conventions.convention: Crossing number is the least crossing count among regular diagrams of the underlying unoriented link type; its definition assumes countable choice.
A reduced alternating link diagram is connected; alternation concerns successive over-under visits on each component, and reducedness excludes a crossing repeated on any region boundary.

Flypes reflect the moving tangle's projection and reverse its crossing data, transporting component orientations. Entire flypes are allowed. Sphere planar isotopies preserve the projection sphere's orientation.
Splitness requires a smooth sphere disjoint from the link with link points on both complementary sides.
Tait vertices are checkerboard regions and edges are crossings joining opposite same-colored sectors; loops and parallel edges are allowed.
In positive braid projection coordinates (t,x), the positive geometric crossing expands as A I + A⁻¹ e_i; the negative crossing expands as A⁻¹ I + A e_i.
Normal transfer is the total inverse image in the normal interval neighborhood boundary, oriented by projection. Definiteness on the zero vector space is allowed.
Span means largest exponent minus smallest exponent of a nonzero Laurent polynomial. Jones specialization uses t=A⁻⁴ and full AC.

load_bearing.statement: For a connected regular link diagram D with c crossings, the Laurent-polynomial span of its Kauffman bracket is at most 4c. If D is reduced and alternating, then changing any one crossing from the all-A state or the all-B state merges two distinct state circles, both extreme coefficients are nonzero, and the bracket span is exactly 4c.
If a regular link diagram on S² is connected and alternating, then the represented link is nonsplit.

A compact connected smoothly embedded surface F in S³ with nonempty boundary L and a supplied finite disk-and-band presentation has nonsplit boundary if a positive or negative definite quadratic form on H₁(F;Q) satisfies q([c])=lk(c,τc) for every oriented rational multicurve c in its interior. Nonorientable surfaces and zero-dimensional definite forms are allowed.

For either checkerboard color of a connected alternating regular diagram, the disk-and-half-twisted-band construction gives a compact connected embedded spanning surface. Its normal-transfer quadratic form is ε times the sum of squared graph-cycle coefficients for a single sign ε; the crossingless case uses a spanning disk and the zero-dimensional definite form.
If the underlying projection of a nonempty regular link diagram on S² is disconnected, then the represented link is split.
Assume ACω. Every connected reduced alternating diagram D of an oriented link L realizes the crossing number of its underlying unoriented link: c(D)=c(L).

Assume full AC and let D be a connected reduced alternating diagram with c crossings. It is A- and B-adequate and has bracket A-span 4c. If D represents a knot K, its library Jones polynomial has t-span c, while every c′-crossing diagram of K has t-span at most c′, with t=A⁻⁴.

Assume full AC. Any two connected reduced alternating diagrams on the oriented projection sphere that represent the same oriented link type are related by a finite sequence of sphere planar isotopies and flypes. Composite links are included; the diagrams are required to be connected, and a plane drawing is interpreted as a punctured projection sphere.

published_dependencies.used_for: Smooth finite link types, ambient isotopy, orientation transport, and moving representatives off infinity.
Finite transverse crossings, over-under data, projection graphs, and crossingless components.
The declared ACω hypothesis for regular projections, crossing number, and bracket invariance.
Nonemptiness of the crossing-count set under ACω.
Existence of the least crossing count.
The positive geometric generator, its reflected inverse, and the worked braid diagrams.
Separation and side-homology calculations for the capped orientable surface in the definite-pairing proof.
Vanishing of H₁(S³;Q) and H₂(S³;Q), and the connected H₀ calculation.
Finite surface-chain arguments and identification of graph-cycle homology.
Transport of decorated diagrams; the flyping item explicitly distinguishes sphere planar isotopy.
The full-AC branches of flyping, Jones specialization, and the examples.
Closure connectivity from endpoint-permutation cycles and the explicit finite-word closure convention.
The kink counterexample represents the unknot after a type-I deletion.

seams_checked.note: The determinant sign, positive Artin generator, and writhe conventions agree with the supplier. The local smoothing calculation explicitly accounts for positive projection coordinates (t,x). No framing conclusion is used without its hypotheses.

The state weights, loop value, writhe normalization, ACω invariance hypothesis, full-AC Jones comparison, and substitution t=A⁻⁴ are preserved. The trefoil and figure-eight computations match these conventions.

The downstream remark uses the least regular-diagram crossing-count definition with its ACω qualification. It does not extend the alternating Jones-span theorem to arbitrary knots or treat the reported Jones-detection claim as an established theorem.
